questions.q: Why does the author call a steady paycheck risky?
a: It leaves your whole career at the mercy of one employer
Salaries rarely keep up with the cost of living
Regular work leaves no time to build skills
Employers prefer to hire freelancers instead
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that relying on one employer hands control of your income to someone else.

questions.q: What does the summary mean by gatekeepers giving you the illusion of freedom?
a: They offer choices within limits they set, leaving the important rules untouched
They promise promotions they never intend to grant
They let you work remotely but cut your pay
They encourage you to start your own business
questions.why: Lesson 2 says gatekeepers hand you a set of options while deciding the things that really matter.

questions.q: What did Tim DeChristopher do at the land auction?
a: He signed up and outbid everyone without the money, and the sale was revoked
He paid the $1.7 million entry fee and bought the land
He organized a protest that shut the auction down
He sued the Bureau of Land Management and won
questions.why: Lesson 2 tells how his bid exposed the unfair sale, which was later invalidated and the land protected.

questions.q: What is legacy work in the summary?
a: Work that uses your skills to help others and outlasts you
Work that builds a large inheritance for your family
Work you can hand over to a successor when you retire
Work that earns enough to let you stop early
questions.why: Lesson 3 defines legacy work as applying your particular abilities to help others long after you are gone.

questions.q: What tip does the summary give for tracking legacy work?
a: Set a measurable target, such as a number of words or hours per day
Wait until you have enough savings to begin
Ask a mentor to review it once a year
Keep it private until it is finished
questions.why: Lesson 3's pro tip suggests a concrete metric like 1,000 words a day or an hour of charity work.
